newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian forces hit outskirts of opposition town.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian forces hit outskirts of opposition town.

text.p: Cambodian government forces on Monday moved to within one kilometre (half a mile) of the last town held by loyalists of ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, military officials said.

"We are one kilometre from O'Smach. We are still one kilometre out because of dense forest, a proliferation of landmines and troops falling sick with malaria," General Meas Sophea, chief of fighting operations, told Reuters.
"We are very near," said Defence Ministry spokesman Chum Sambath said. O'Smach is close to Cambodia's northwestern border with Thailand.
"We hope that very, very soon, O'Smach will fall into government hands," he said.

The Khmer Rouge, which Thai military sources said had sent troops to reinforce royalist positions in O'Smach, on Monday appealed to opposition forces to press its fight against the country's leader, Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.

"The task of the whole nation, people and all resistance movement forces is to join together to fight by all means against the puppet Hun Sen...to end the war completely," it broadcast on its clandestine radio, for years the propaganda mouthpiece of the Maoist rebels.
Last week, the Khmer Rouge said it had formed a military alliance against Hun Sen that included General Nhiek Bun Chhay, Ranariddh's senior military commander.
Ranariddh has denied any royalist alliance with the movement, which ruled Cambodia during the 1975-79 "Killing Fields" years.
Ranariddh's rag-tag forces have been fighting the government in the northwest since the prince was overthrown by Hun Sen on July 6.

Since then, Ranariddh's forces have been driven back to the northwest and now control only O'Smach town and a small strip of territory along the Thai border leading to the Khmer Rouge base of Anlong Veng, about 50 km (39 miles) east of O'Smach, Cambodian army officials said.

Hun Sen and Ranariddh formed an uneasy coalition after 1993 elections sponsored by the United Nations. The Khmer Rouge was a party to the 1991 pact that led to the polls but reneged on the deal and waged a low-intensity guerrilla war against Phnom Penh.
Ranariddh had been negotiating a peace deal with the guerrillas for several months and was reported to have reached an agreement just before Hun Sen's power grab.
Forces loyal to Hun Sen pounded O'Smach with mortar and artillery fire at the weekend.

At least 22 mortar rounds and nine artillery shells landed in the town's outskirts on Sunday morning and the Thai army had been moved to full alert in case the fighting or shelling spilled across the Thai border, a Thai army commander said.
A colonel in Siem Reap said about 5,000 government troops were now in the O'Smach area.

Information on royalist casualties was not available, but several government soldiers have been killed. Dozens more have been injured by mines and artillery or fallen sick with malaria, officials said.
